memos.headline: ARI liquidating: last NYSE trade Nov 6, $4.10 cash paid Oct 29, stock 6.39
reasoning: Quote: 'intends to file a Form 25 ... relating to the delisting ... on or about October 27, 2026 ... the last day of trading on the NYSE will be November 6, 2026'
Original source (Oct 9 release): initial liquidating distribution of $4.10 per share payable Oct 29, record Oct 20, due bills until Oct 29, ex-date Oct 30
Original source (liquidation proxy): estimated total liquidating distributions $7.75-$8.50 per share, complete by first half of 2028
What changed Friday: a hard date after which the shares stop trading on an exchange
Stock 6.39 Friday; 30-day mean gap 0.34%, pinned
objections: SCOUT: the liquidation and the $4.10 were public; only the delisting date is new

memos.headline: Long ARI: 6.39 buys an estimated 7.75-8.50 of cash, 21-33% gross
reasoning: Buyer at 6.39 gets 4.10 on Oct 29, leaving a stub priced at 2.29 against an estimated 3.65-4.40 still to come
The first payout came in above the proxy's 3.70-4.00 range, which supports the top half of the estimate
What the market must believe: the stub is worth about 2.29, a 37-48% haircut to management's estimate, for illiquidity and CRE credit risk
Delisting forces index funds and exchange-only holders out by Nov 6, which can push the price lower into the deadline
Holding period: the edge is only realized by holding into the liquidation through 2028. A position inside this crew's reach ends by Nov 6
Wrong if: CRE asset sales come in below book, or the stub keeps trading at a discount through Nov 6
objections: SCOUT: only the delisting date is new (open)

memos.headline: The discount is real but it is the price of a two-year illiquid stub
reasoning: ANALYST is right that 2.29 for an estimated 3.65-4.40 is a wide discount; I cannot call it obviously priced in
But the estimate dates from August and assumes asset sales into a market where CRE delinquencies are rising
After Nov 6 the stub cannot be sold on an exchange; holders wait until 2028 for the rest. That alone justifies a big discount
Inside the 14 trading days this crew can hold, the thesis has no catalyst: the stub's value is not decided before Nov 6
Track record: 3 past cases, none with 5 days of history. Nothing to lean on yet
I let it through to QUANT with objections on record, because the numbers decide this one
objections: SCOUT: only the delisting date is new (open)
SKEPTIC 1: the 7.75-8.50 estimate is from August and assumes CRE sales hold up
SKEPTIC 2: no catalyst inside a 14-day holding window
SKEPTIC 3: the stub becomes illiquid after Nov 6

memos.headline: No bracket can hold this. The Oct 30 ex-date alone fires any stop.
reasoning: Entry would be about 6.39 (Friday close; the weekend quote of 5.47/7.39 is not a real market)
On Oct 30 the stock goes ex the $4.10 payout and should open near 2.29. Any stop above that fires mechanically on that day
The paper account does not reliably pay out liquidating distributions, so that fill would book a fake loss of about 4.10 a share: about $3,200 on a $5,000 position
Exit before Oct 30 gives up the payout, and with no catalyst before then the expected move is near zero minus the spread
Holding past Nov 6 is impossible: the shares stop trading, and the time limit and bracket legs cannot close them
No size gives positive expectancy inside this crew's tools. p_strike near 1.0 for any stop placed before the ex-date
objections: SCOUT: only the delisting date is new (open)
SKEPTIC 1: estimate from August (open)
SKEPTIC 2: no catalyst inside 14 days (accepted)
SKEPTIC 3: stub illiquid after Nov 6 (accepted)
QUANT: a large distribution plus delisting cannot be expressed as a bracket order

memos.headline: Case 04 ARI: no trade. Real discount, wrong tool. QUANT stopped it.
reasoning: SCOUT: liquidation, $4.10 paid Oct 29, last trade Nov 6, estimated 7.75-8.50 total by 2028
ANALYST: long for a 21-33% gross discount to the estimate, realized only by holding into 2028
SKEPTIC: let it through with three objections; the discount is the price of illiquidity
QUANT: objected. The ex-date drop fires any stop, the paper account would book a fake loss, and nothing can be held past Nov 6
Lesson for SCOUT: skip liquidations with a large distribution or a delisting date inside the holding window
Check: ARI price into Oct 29 and Nov 6; size of the second liquidating distribution when declared
